## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The changed line fixes the abort reported in #12858. With `OMARCHY_PATH` unset or empty, `omarchy-update-dev` now takes the packaged early exit instead of failing under `set -u`. A set, non-empty checkout path still validates and pulls exactly as before. The new test passes on this head and fails when run against the base script, which stops with `line 7: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable`.

| `OMARCHY_PATH` | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unset | exits 1, unbound variable | exits 0, no git call |
| empty (`OMARCHY_PATH=`) | runs `git -C "" ...` in the current directory | exits 0, no git call |
| `/usr/share/omarchy` | exits 0, no git call | exits 0, no git call |
| dev checkout path | pulls that checkout | pulls that checkout |

The empty-value row is a side benefit that the PR doesn't mention: git treats `-C ""` as "stay in the current directory". So on the base, `OMARCHY_PATH=` could fast-forward whatever clone the update was started from. A synthetic case with a real clone showed exactly that.

### `sudo omarchy update` now continues into package and migration steps as root

The PR description and the new code comment name `sudo omarchy update` as a motivating case. Under default sudo settings, `env_reset` drops `OMARCHY_PATH` and sets `HOME` to root's home. On the base, the update ran its preparation steps as root and then stopped at `omarchy-update-dev`. With this change, that stop is gone, and the rest of `bin/omarchy-update` runs as root:

```text
sudo omarchy update   (OMARCHY_PATH unset, HOME=/root)
  prune cache, snapshot, stay-awake       base: runs    head: runs
  omarchy-update-dev                      base: exit 1  head: exit 0 (skips)
  keyring, system packages                base: -       head: runs as root
  omarchy-migrate                         base: -       head: runs as root
    reads /usr/share/omarchy/migrations
    marker state in /root/.local/state/omarchy/migrations
  post-update hook, AUR, mise, orphans    base: -       head: runs as root
```

Nothing in `omarchy`, `omarchy-update` or `omarchy-migrate` refuses to run as root. `docs/update-process.md` states that migrations run per-user because they may need `$HOME` and session state.

**Impact:** root usually has no migration markers, so every packaged migration counts as pending. The whole history then replays against root's home, and the invoking user's own migration state stays untouched. Some old migrations repeat system-wide package changes; `1780739888.sh`, for example, removes `dust` again. This comes from source tracing only. How far a real root run gets was not tested.

**Suggested change:** refuse to run `omarchy-update` as root, as `bin/omarchy-dev-link` already does (`if (( EUID == 0 )); then ... exit 1; fi`). Alternatively, drop `sudo` from the stated motivation so the fix covers only non-root stripped environments such as cron, timers and non-login shells.

### Dev-linked systems skip the checkout pull silently when the variable is missing

On a machine set up with `omarchy-dev-link`, `/etc/omarchy.conf` records the checkout path, and `default/bash/env-bootstrap` treats that file as the source of truth. The new fallback ignores it, and `omarchy-migrate` also defaults to `/usr/share/omarchy/migrations`.

**Impact:** if `OMARCHY_PATH` is missing (a non-login shell, for example), the checkout is not pulled and nothing is printed. The update then continues as a packaged update, with packaged migrations. Before this change, the same run aborted visibly.

**Suggested change:** resolve the path the way `env-bootstrap` does (read `/etc/omarchy.conf` before falling back to `/usr/share/omarchy`), or print a one-line notice when the fallback is used.

**Scope note:** the same `omarchy update` run still prints `omarchy-update-available: line 9: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable`, via `omarchy-update-status`. That error isn't fatal, but it is reported as "no update available". The discussion on #12858 lists that script and others with the same pattern, so `Fixes #12858` would close the issue while they remain. Two related open PRs overlap this one: #8590 makes the equivalent `omarchy-update-dev` change, and #12860 contains the identical line and also changes `omarchy-update-available` and `omarchy-channel-current`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** The changed script and the PR's test were run in a sandbox on the head and the base, with bash 5.3.15 and git 2.55.0. The runs used a logging git stub, one real-git case with a synthetic clone for the empty value, and `test/shell` on single-test trees. `omarchy-update-status` was also probed with the variable unset. The `sudo` and dev-link paths through the full `omarchy update` pipeline were assessed from source and the sudoers documentation only. No real update, package transaction or root run was executed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
